decision: Where and how should the owned report show the first four real pages of the child's Workbook 1, with the action 'Start your plan today'?
primary_axis: placement in the report story (information hierarchy)
invariants: the same four pages: cover, the first lesson with its worked example, two practice pages of the first topic
real rendered page images (here a fake U4 sample; live pages carry the child's own name)
the D-305 report order: where the child is, what's in workbook 1, the next step
the existing report tokens and rows (src/components/report.css)
one action, 'Start your plan today', that goes to the existing plan choice and card step; approved free-month line from D-312

options.bet: The pages lead the 'What's in workbook 1' row, above the plan summary
options.benefit: One row answers 'what will my child get' with the plan and the proof together
options.cost: The row becomes very long; the plan summary falls below the fold
options.risk: A second button inside a summary row competes with the Next step row

options.bet: A row of its own, '{child}'s first pages', right after 'What's in workbook 1' and right before Next step
options.benefit: The real pages sit between the plan and the ask; the cover is larger, so the child's name reads first; on a phone one swipe strip keeps it to one screen
options.cost: One more row on a long page
options.risk: A parent who stops after the plan summary never scrolls to it (it is still above the next step)

options.bet: The pages sit inside the Next step row, above the plan button
options.cost: The next step row changes for every state (saved card, waitlist, dashboard rail) and becomes heavy
options.risk: On the dashboard the next step lives in the side rail, where four pages do not fit

selection.status: agent-recommended; Savar approves the UI on the pull request before merge
